title: Shift Run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean to each of four query indices and each finite bit string, let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $q$ be one of the three search phases, let $S$ be a machine state, let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory function, and let $p\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose $0\le p\le P$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, $S.Z=0$, and $S.K\,2^{S.C}\le B$. Then the machine has a finite run from shift phase $0$ for phase $q$ to the first copy phase for that same phase, with every configuration satisfying $G(x,B,P)$. At the endpoint the shift counter is zero, $K=S.K\,2^{S.C}$ (using the initial values in $S$), and all other registers, the memory function, and the memory-head position are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: an oracle family on four query indices and bit strings
a phase $q$ among the three search phases
a memory-head position $p\in\mathbb Z$ with $0\le p\le P$
every register of $S$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ be a family of four Boolean oracles on bit
strings, let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $q$ be one of the three phases, let $S$ be
a register state, and let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory
tape with head position $p\in\mathbb Z$. Assume $0\le p\le P$, every register of $S$ is
at most $B$, the scratch register of $S$ is zero, and $S.K\,2^{S.C}\le B$. Then the
machine $A(K_0)$ has a finite run from shift phase $0$ in phase $q$, with every
intermediate configuration satisfying $G(x,B,P)$, to the first copy phase for the same
phase, with the shift counter reset to zero and the register $K$ set to its initial
value times $2$ raised to its initial shift counter; all other registers, the tape, and
the head position are unchanged.
